lessons.text: Before submitting, compare every port, parameter and module name in the task prompt and the spec's interface tables with your top module; the hidden testbench reads them by exactly those names.
Keep the clock and reset names the spec uses (for example a bus clock named in the spec) instead of generic names like clk or rst.
When the spec describes internal registers or a state machine by name, declare them with those names at the top level of the module; tests may read them.
Do not stop at a clean compile: write a small self-checking testbench that drives the spec's examples and corner cases, and compare against expected values.
Compile with every file the task lists, using the top module the task names, so the build matches what the hidden tests will run.
If your own testbench passes on the first try, add a check for reset values, back-to-back transactions and the widest parameter values before submitting.
When the task says to reuse existing modules, instantiate them with their existing port names and parameters rather than rewriting them.
Keep parameters overridable (declare them as module parameters with the spec's defaults) so a test can set them by name.
